title: How often must customer due diligence data be updated under the EU AML Regulation (AMLR)? | Customer Due Diligence Guide
summary: Article 26 AMLR: update CDD data at least yearly for higher-risk customers and every 5 years for others, plus event-driven reviews and what to record.
body_markdown:
*What Article 26 AMLR requires, what AMLA's draft guidelines on ongoing monitoring add, and how eIDs keep customer data current.*


Under Article 26 of the EU Anti-Money Laundering Regulation (AMLR), obliged entities must update customer due diligence data at least every year for higher-risk customers subject to enhanced due diligence and at least every 5 years for all other customers.


Customer information must also be reviewed when the customer's relevant circumstances change or when the obliged entity becomes aware of a relevant fact. The AMLR applies from 10 July 2027.


*Written by Aleksander Wasiak (Compliance Officer) and Helena Suska (Head of Customer Success), Authologic.*
